references.text: God gives Abraham the covenant of circumcision, establishing the practice of circumcising all male children as a sign of the covenant between God and Abraham's descendants.
Abraham circumcised his son Isaac when he was eight days old, as God had commanded him, demonstrating the first fulfillment of the command to circumcise on the eighth day.
Joshua circumcised the Israelites at Gilgal after that generation born in the wilderness had not been circumcised, reaffirming the importance of circumcision as a sign of the covenant.
John the Baptist was circumcised on the eighth day in accordance with the Mosaic Law, showing that this practice continued to be observed in New Testament times.
Jesus was circumcised on the eighth day and given his name, directly fulfilling Leviticus 12:3 and demonstrating Mary's and Joseph's faithfulness to the law.
Jesus refers to circumcision on the eighth day in his discussion with the Jews, pointing out that circumcision is performed even on the Sabbath to fulfill the Mosaic Law.
Stephen mentions in his speech that God gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision, and that Abraham circumcised Isaac on the eighth day.
Paul notes that he himself was circumcised on the eighth day, highlighting his Jewish heritage and fulfillment of the law from birth.
